title: Dilu: Enabling GPU Resourcing-on-Demand for Serverless DL Serving via Introspective Elasticity
problem: Serverless DL serving systems use coarse-grained static GPU allocation that produces 15-94% GPU fragmentation due to dynamic workload patterns; existing horizontal-only scaling cannot adapt GPU resource allocation fine-grainedly within a running DL function instance, degrading utilization and violating QoS.
motivation: Large language model serving on serverless GPU infrastructure is expensive and fragmentation-prone, and the inability to dynamically right-size GPU resources within a function (without full cold restart) prevents efficient multiplexing and SLA compliance.
method: Dilu introduces Introspective Elasticity, a system that adjusts GPU resources in two ways: within each running task (changing compute and memory allocation) and across multiple instances (adding or removing copies). To do this, it profiles how sensitive each deep-learning function is to compute and memory constraints, then uses a scheduler to pack compatible tasks together to fill up wasted GPU space on the hardware. At runtime, a controller continuously watches whether tasks are meeting their performance targets and adjusts both the per-task GPU allocation and the number of instances to reduce GPU waste while keeping all tasks meeting their performance goals.
key_novelty: Introspective Elasticity enables real-time, two-dimensional GPU resource adjustment for serverless deep-learning functions without restarting, eliminating the static allocation that causes GPU fragmentation.
contributions: Introspective Elasticity (IE): two-dimensional GPU co-scaling (vertical + horizontal) for serverless DL tasks
Multi-factor profiling with pruning search for efficient DL task resource sensitivity characterization
Resourcing-complementary scheduling principle for filling GPU fragments with compatible DL tasks
10-46% GPU defragmentation, up to 1.8x inference throughput, and 11-71% QoS violation rate reduction vs SOTA

metrics.speedup: up to 1.8x inference throughput; 1.1x training throughput improvement
metrics.other: 10-46% GPU defragmentation; 11-71% QoS violation rate reduction vs SOTA baselines

baselines: state-of-the-art serverless DL GPU serving systems
limitations: The 2D co-scaling controller adds profiling and runtime monitoring overhead; effectiveness for extremely short-lived DL functions with rapid workload shifts not characterized.
primary_theme: Two-dimensional GPU elasticity for serverless DL serving
